title: Trace an argument: set 2

examples.question: Phones Away An original passage written for LearnAce 1 Phones should be banned from classrooms during instructional time. The evidence that they harm learning is strong, and the solution is simple. 2 Attention is limited. In one widely cited experiment, the mere presence of a smartphone on a desk — even turned off and face down — reduced performance on tests of memory and problem-solving. Notifications, when allowed, fragment attention further. 3 Supporters of phones in class point out that they can be useful tools for research or calculation. That is true, but schools already provide devices for those purposes, which can be managed and filtered in ways personal phones cannot. 4 A ban also removes a burden from teachers, who currently spend valuable minutes policing phone use, and from students, many of whom report feeling relieved when the decision to disconnect is made for them. What is the author's claim?
examples.answer: Phones should be banned from classrooms during instructional time
choices: Phones should be banned from classrooms during instructional time

examples.question: Votes at Sixteen An original passage written for LearnAce 1 Canada should lower the federal voting age to sixteen. Young people are affected by government decisions on climate, education and the economy for longer than anyone, yet they have no say in choosing the people who make those decisions. 2 Critics argue that sixteen-year-olds lack the maturity to vote. But research on "cold cognition" — careful decision-making without time pressure — shows that by sixteen, most people reason about as well as adults. Voting, which allows weeks of reflection, depends on precisely this kind of thinking. 3 Evidence from places that have lowered the voting age is encouraging. After Austria allowed sixteen-year-olds to vote in 2007, studies found that their turnout was higher than that of voters aged eighteen to twenty, and their political knowledge was comparable. 4 Habits formed early tend to last. People who vote in the first election for which they are eligible are more likely to keep voting for life. Letting students cast a first ballot while still living at home and learning civics in school could build a lifelong habit of participation. Which finding would most weaken the argument?
examples.answer: A study showing sixteen-year-old voters made less-informed choices than older voters
choices: A study showing sixteen-year-old voters made less-informed choices than older voters
